Vanessa / team — see proposed redline language below and brief rationale. I kept the commercial compromise pragmatic while protecting against open-ended obligations. Please review and flag anything that would be a deal-breaker for Sales before I send to Acme.

Proposed text (MSA Section 13 - Limitation of Liability):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the aggregate liability of Redwood Inference to Customer for any and all claims arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) Two Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (USD $250,000) or (b) the total fees paid by Customer to Redwood Inference under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. The foregoing limitation shall not apply to (i) Customer's indemnification obligations for third-party claims of intellectual property infringement; (ii) damages arising from Redwood's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud; (iii) Customer's claims for equitable relief; or (iv) liabilities that are statutorily required to be uncapped (including certain regulatory fines arising from data-security breaches)."

Proposed text (Termination / Prepaid Fees):
"If Customer terminates this Agreement for convenience, Redwood will refund Customer on a pro rata basis the portion of any prepaid, unused fees attributable to the remainder of the then-current prepaid period, less (i) any unpaid amounts owed to Redwood for services already provided and (ii) reasonable wind-down costs reasonably incurred by Redwood in connection with the termination (the "Net Refund"). The aggregate Net Refund payable under this Section shall be subject to the Limitation of Liability set forth in Section 13."

Proposed text (Wind-down Assistance):
"Upon termination for convenience, Redwood will provide up to thirty (30) days of reasonable wind-down assistance at no additional charge to support export of Customer data and transition activities. Redwood will make available additional transition services at Redwood's then-current professional services rates upon Customer request."

Rationale (short):
- The $250k floor preserves a minimum recovery for smaller deals while tying catastrophic exposure to actual economic activity for larger deployments.
- Carve-outs keep Redwood responsible for intentional or egregious misconduct and IP infringement.
- Attaching the refund to the LoL cap prevents repayment obligations from creating uncapped exposure; the Net Refund is still recoverable but cannot exceed the LoL.
- Limiting included wind-down assistance to 30 days prevents an open-ended, resource-intensive obligation; customers can buy extra time.

If Sales is comfortable, I'll insert these redlines into RWI_MSA_redline_20260923.pdf and send to Acme with a short explanatory note.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Alice — thanks for the clear list. Attached is a redline of the MSA (RWI_MSA_redline_20260923.pdf) that reflects the compromise language from our legal team. Highlights:

- Limitation of Liability: cap = greater of $250k or fees paid in prior 12 months; standard carve-outs for IP, willful misconduct, and statutorily uncapped regulatory liabilities.
- Prepaid refunds: Redwood will issue a pro-rata refund of unused prepaid fees on termination for convenience, net of reasonable wind-down costs and outstanding amounts. This Net Refund will be subject to the LoL cap above.
- Wind-down assistance: 30 days included; additional days available at standard PS rates.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached redline and confirm whether Acme can accept the Net Refund being subject to the LoL cap.
2) If OK, confirm any additional wind-down requirements (e.g., SFTP export, format, timing).

If Acme would prefer to keep refunds uncapped (i.e., outside the LoL cap), we can escalate for an exceptions review but will likely need additional commercial consideration (e.g., higher fees or an escrow arrangement).

I've attached the redline and a copy of the Order Form for reference. If you'd like, we can schedule a 20-minute call to walk through the changes — I have availability Monday morning.
